```{r Step 1, Set-up, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# BLS ECEC Industry Benefits
# 2000-2024
#
# Uses blsR to access the BLS Public Data API
#
# Primary source:
#   Employer Costs for Employee Compensation (ECEC)
#
# Population:
#   Private industry workers
#
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(blsR)
library(here)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Check BLS API key
# ------------------------------------------------------------

bls_api_key <- Sys.getenv("BLS_API_KEY")

if (bls_api_key == "") {
  stop(
    "BLS API key not found. Check that bls_api_key is stored ",
    "in your .Renviron file."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define broad industry categories
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_codes <- tribble(
  ~industry_code, ~industry,
  "2300", "Construction",
  "3000", "Manufacturing",
  "4000", "Trade, transportation, and utilities",
  "4110", "Wholesale trade",
  "4120", "Retail trade",
  "4300", "Transportation and warehousing",
  "5100", "Information",
  "5200", "Finance and insurance",
  "5300", "Real estate and rental and leasing",
  "5400", "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
  "5600", "Administrative and support and waste management and remediation services",
  "6000", "Education and health services",
  "6100", "Educational services",
  "6200", "Health care and social assistance",
  "7000", "Leisure and hospitality",
  "7200", "Accommodation and food services",
  "8100", "Other services except public administration"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define ECEC benefit categories
# ------------------------------------------------------------

benefit_codes <- tribble(
  ~estimate_code, ~benefit,
  "03", "Total benefits",
  "04", "Paid leave",
  "13", "Insurance",
  "15", "Health insurance",
  "18", "Retirement and savings",
  "21", "Legally required benefits"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Construct ECEC series IDs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

series_lookup <- crossing(
  benefit_codes,
  industry_codes
) %>%
  mutate(
    series_id = paste0(
      "CMU",
      "2",
      estimate_code,
      industry_code,
      "000",
      "000",
      "D"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    series_id,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    industry_code,
    industry
  )

series_lookup
```

```{r Step 2, Pull-in, include=TRUE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
# 2. Define industries 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
industry_codes <- tribble( 
  ~industry_code, ~industry, 
  "2300", "Construction", 
  "3000", "Manufacturing", 
  "4000", "Trade, transportation, and utilities", 
  "4110", "Wholesale trade", 
  "4120", "Retail trade", 
  "4300", "Transportation and warehousing", 
  "5100", "Information", 
  "5200", "Finance and insurance", 
  "5300", "Real estate and rental and leasing", 
  "5400", "Professional, scientific, and technical services", 
  "5600", "Administrative and support and waste management and remediation services", 
  "6000", "Education and health services", 
  "6100", "Educational services", 
  "6200", "Health care and social assistance", 
  "7000", "Leisure and hospitality", 
  "7200", "Accommodation and food services", 
  "8100", "Other services except public administration" 
  ) 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
# 3. Define benefit measures 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
benefit_codes <- tribble( 
  ~estimate_code, ~benefit, 
  "03", "Total benefits", 
  "04", "Paid leave", 
  "13", "Insurance", 
  "15", "Health insurance", 
  "18", "Retirement and savings", 
  "21", "Legally required benefits" 
  ) 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
# 4. Construct ECEC series IDs # 
# Structure: # CMU # 2 = private industry # 03 = estimate # 2300 = industry # 000 = all occupations # 000 = all workers # D = cost per hour worked 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
series_lookup <- crossing( benefit_codes, industry_codes ) %>% 
  mutate( 
    series_id = paste0( 
      "CMU", 
      "2", 
      estimate_code, 
      industry_code, 
      "000",
      "000", 
      "D" ) 
    ) %>% 
  select( 
    series_id, estimate_code, benefit, industry_code, industry 
    ) 
# Inspect the first few IDs before making any request 

series_lookup %>% slice_head(n = 20) 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
# 5. FIRST TEST: 
# Retrieve three known basic benefit series 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 

test_series <- c( 
  "CMU2030000000000D", # Private industry, total benefits 
  "CMU2032300000000D", # Construction, total benefits 
  "CMU2033000000000D" # Manufacturing, total benefits 
  ) 

test_ecec <- get_n_series_table( 
  test_series, start_year = 2004, end_year = 2024, api_key = bls_api_key ) 

# Inspect result 
test_ecec 

# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
# 6. Convert test result to long format 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 

test_ecec_long <- test_ecec %>% 
  pivot_longer( 
    cols = all_of(test_series), names_to = "series_id", values_to = "value" ) %>% 
  mutate( value = as.numeric(value) ) %>% 
  left_join( series_lookup, by = "series_id" ) 

test_ecec_long 

# ------------------------------------------------------------ 
# 7. Check whether the test returned observations 
# ------------------------------------------------------------ 

test_ecec_long %>% 
  group_by(series_id, industry, benefit) %>% 
  summarise( n_obs = sum(!is.na(value)), first_year = min(year[value %>% is.finite()], na.rm = TRUE), 
             last_year = max(year[value %>% is.finite()], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" )
```

```{r Step 4, Full Pull, include=TRUE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define industries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_codes <- tribble(
  ~industry_code, ~industry,
  "2300", "Construction",
  "3000", "Manufacturing",
  "4000", "Trade, transportation, and utilities",
  "4110", "Wholesale trade",
  "4120", "Retail trade",
  "4300", "Transportation and warehousing",
  "5100", "Information",
  "5200", "Finance and insurance",
  "5300", "Real estate and rental and leasing",
  "5400", "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
  "5600", "Administrative and support and waste management and remediation services",
  "6000", "Education and health services",
  "6100", "Educational services",
  "6200", "Health care and social assistance",
  "7000", "Leisure and hospitality",
  "7200", "Accommodation and food services",
  "8100", "Other services except public administration"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define benefit measures
# ------------------------------------------------------------

benefit_codes <- tribble(
  ~estimate_code, ~benefit,
  "03", "Total benefits",
  "04", "Paid leave",
  "13", "Insurance",
  "15", "Health insurance",
  "18", "Retirement and savings",
  "21", "Legally required benefits"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Construct candidate series IDs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

series_lookup <- crossing(
  benefit_codes,
  industry_codes
) %>%
  mutate(
    series_id = paste0(
      "CMU",
      "2",               # private industry
      estimate_code,
      industry_code,
      "000",             # all occupations
      "000",             # all workers
      "D"                # cost per hour worked
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    series_id,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    industry_code,
    industry
  )

# Check
series_lookup
nrow(series_lookup)

# Expected:
# 17 industries x 6 benefit measures = 102 series


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Function to validate one BLS series
#
# We deliberately query each series separately here.
# This lets us distinguish:
#   - valid series with observations
#   - valid series with no observations
#   - nonexistent/unavailable series
#
# rather than allowing one problematic series to crash
# a large batch request.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

validate_ecec_series <- function(series_id,
                                 start_year = 2004,
                                 end_year = 2024,
                                 api_key = bls_api_key) {

  result <- tryCatch(

    {
      x <- get_n_series_table(
        series_id,
        start_year = start_year,
        end_year = end_year,
        api_key = api_key
      )

      # Find the returned series column
      if (!series_id %in% names(x)) {
        return(
          tibble(
            series_id = series_id,
            status = "no_series_column",
            n_obs = NA_integer_,
            first_year = NA_integer_,
            last_year = NA_integer_
          )
        )
      }

      values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x[[series_id]]))

      valid_values <- values[is.finite(values)]

      if (length(valid_values) == 0) {
        tibble(
          series_id = series_id,
          status = "no_observations",
          n_obs = 0L,
          first_year = NA_integer_,
          last_year = NA_integer_
        )
      } else {

        year_values <- x$year[is.finite(values)]

        tibble(
          series_id = series_id,
          status = "available",
          n_obs = length(valid_values),
          first_year = min(year_values, na.rm = TRUE),
          last_year = max(year_values, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
      }
    },

    error = function(e) {

      tibble(
        series_id = series_id,
        status = paste0("error: ", conditionMessage(e)),
        n_obs = NA_integer_,
        first_year = NA_integer_,
        last_year = NA_integer_
      )
    }
  )

  result
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Validate all 102 candidate series
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ecec_validation <- map_dfr(
  series_lookup$series_id,
  validate_ecec_series
)

# Attach labels
ecec_validation <- ecec_validation %>%
  left_join(
    series_lookup,
    by = "series_id"
  ) %>%
  select(
    series_id,
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    everything()
  )

# Inspect
ecec_validation


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Validation summary
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ecec_validation %>%
  count(status)

ecec_validation %>%
  filter(status != "available") %>%
  select(
    series_id,
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    status
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Save validation table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dir.create(
  here("01_tidydata", "BLS_ECEC"),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

write_csv(
  ecec_validation,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_series_validation_2004_2024.csv"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  ecec_validation,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_series_validation_2004_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Identify usable series
# ------------------------------------------------------------

valid_series <- ecec_validation %>%
  filter(status == "available") %>%
  pull(series_id)

length(valid_series)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Pull valid series
#
# BLS API permits multiple series in one request, but we
# divide the request into batches to avoid another failure
# from an overly large request.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

series_batches <- split(
  valid_series,
  ceiling(seq_along(valid_series) / 25)
)

ecec_raw_list <- map(
  series_batches,
  ~ get_n_series_table(
    .x,
    start_year = 2004,
    end_year = 2024,
    api_key = bls_api_key
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Combine raw API results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ecec_raw <- reduce(
  ecec_raw_list,
  full_join,
  by = "year"
)

# Inspect
glimpse(ecec_raw)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Save raw ECEC extraction
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  ecec_raw,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_benefits_raw_2004_2024.rds"
  )
)

write_csv(
  ecec_raw,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_benefits_raw_2004_2024.csv"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Reshape to tidy industry-year-benefit format
# ------------------------------------------------------------


ecec_raw_list_clean <- map( 
  ecec_raw_list, ~ .x %>% 
    select( year, 
            period, 
            where(is.numeric) ) )

map( ecec_raw_list_clean, ~ dim(.x) )

ecec_raw <- reduce( 
  ecec_raw_list_clean, 
  full_join, by = c("year", "period") )

dim(ecec_raw)


ecec_benefits_quarterly <- ecec_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(year, period),
    names_to = "series_id",
    values_to = "benefit_cost_per_hour"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    benefit_cost_per_hour = as.numeric(benefit_cost_per_hour)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    series_lookup,
    by = "series_id"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry),
    !is.na(benefit)
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    period,
    industry_code,
    estimate_code
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    period,
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    series_id,
    benefit_cost_per_hour
  )

# Inspect
ecec_benefits_quarterly

```

```{r Step 5: Annualize the Data, include=TRUE}
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Annualize ECEC benefits data
# ---------------------------------------------------------

ecec_benefits_annual <- ecec_benefits_quarterly %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    series_id
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    benefit_cost_per_hour = if (all(is.na(benefit_cost_per_hour))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(benefit_cost_per_hour, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    n_quarters = sum(!is.na(benefit_cost_per_hour)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostic checks
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# Dimensions
dim(ecec_benefits_annual)

# Number of industries and observations by benefit
ecec_benefits_annual %>%
  group_by(benefit) %>%
  summarise(
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_code),
    first_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_observations = sum(!is.na(benefit_cost_per_hour)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Number of observations by year
ecec_benefits_annual %>%
  count(year)

# Check number of quarters underlying each annual observation
ecec_benefits_annual %>%
  count(n_quarters)

# Inspect the data
head(ecec_benefits_annual)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Save quarterly and annual versions
# ---------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  ecec_benefits_quarterly,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_benefits_industry_quarterly_2004_2024.rds"
  )
)

write_csv(
  ecec_benefits_quarterly,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_benefits_industry_quarterly_2004_2024.csv"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  ecec_benefits_annual,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_benefits_industry_annual_2004_2024.rds"
  )
)

write_csv(
  ecec_benefits_annual,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "BLS_ECEC",
    "ecec_benefits_industry_annual_2004_2024.csv"
  )
)

# Final validation
ecec_benefits_annual %>%
  summarise(
    min_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_code),
    n_benefits = n_distinct(benefit),
    n_series = n_distinct(series_id),
    observations = n(),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(benefit_cost_per_hour))
  )

# Confirm no duplicate industry-benefit-year observations
ecec_benefits_annual %>%
  count(
    year,
    industry_code,
    estimate_code
  ) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
```

```{r Step 6, Supplementary Pull, include=TRUE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# ECEC WAGES AND SALARIES
# Private industry, all occupations, all workers
# 2004-2024
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ECEC estimate code:
# 02 = Wages and salaries

wage_estimate_code <- "02"

# Build ECEC series IDs
#
# Structure:
# CMU + ownership + estimate + industry + occupation + subcell + datatype
#
# 2    = private industry
# 02   = wages and salaries
# 0000 = industry
# 000  = all occupations
# 000  = all workers
# D    = cost per hour worked

wage_series_lookup <- industry_codes %>%
  mutate(
    estimate_code = wage_estimate_code,
    benefit = "Wages and salaries",
    series_id = paste0(
      "CMU",
      "2",
      estimate_code,
      industry_code,
      "000",
      "000",
      "D"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    series_id
  )

wage_series_lookup




# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DEFINE ECEC SERIES VALIDATION FUNCTION
# ------------------------------------------------------------

validate_ecec_series <- function(series_id,
                                 start_year = 2004,
                                 end_year = 2024,
                                 api_key = bls_api_key) {

  result <- tryCatch(

    {
      x <- get_n_series_table(
        series_id,
        start_year = start_year,
        end_year = end_year,
        api_key = api_key
      )

      # Find the returned series column
      if (!series_id %in% names(x)) {
        return(
          tibble(
            series_id = series_id,
            status = "no_series_column",
            n_obs = NA_integer_,
            first_year = NA_integer_,
            last_year = NA_integer_
          )
        )
      }

      values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x[[series_id]]))

      valid_values <- values[is.finite(values)]

      if (length(valid_values) == 0) {

        tibble(
          series_id = series_id,
          status = "no_observations",
          n_obs = 0L,
          first_year = NA_integer_,
          last_year = NA_integer_
        )

      } else {

        year_values <- x$year[is.finite(values)]

        tibble(
          series_id = series_id,
          status = "available",
          n_obs = length(valid_values),
          first_year = min(year_values, na.rm = TRUE),
          last_year = max(year_values, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
      }
    },

    error = function(e) {

      tibble(
        series_id = series_id,
        status = paste0("error: ", conditionMessage(e)),
        n_obs = NA_integer_,
        first_year = NA_integer_,
        last_year = NA_integer_
      )
    }
  )

  result
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# VALIDATE WAGE SERIES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

wage_validation <- map_dfr(
  wage_series_lookup$series_id,
  ~ validate_ecec_series(
    series_id = .x,
    start_year = 2004,
    end_year = 2024,
    api_key = bls_api_key
  )
) %>%
  left_join(
    wage_series_lookup,
    by = "series_id"
  ) %>%
  select(
    series_id,
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    benefit,
    status,
    n_obs,
    first_year,
    last_year
  )

wage_validation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CHECK RESULTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

wage_validation %>%
  count(status)

wage_validation %>%
  filter(status != "available")

wage_validation %>%
  filter(status == "available") %>%
  count(n_obs)
```

```{r Step 7, Full Supplemental Pull, include=TRUE}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PULL ECEC WAGES AND SALARIES
# 2004-2024
# ------------------------------------------------------------

valid_wage_series <- wage_validation %>%
  filter(status == "available") %>%
  pull(series_id)

length(valid_wage_series)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# BATCH THE SERIES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

wage_series_batches <- split(
  valid_wage_series,
  ceiling(seq_along(valid_wage_series) / 25)
)

length(wage_series_batches)



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PULL EACH BATCH
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ecec_wage_raw_list <- map(
  seq_along(wage_series_batches),
  function(i) {

    message(
      "Pulling wage batch ",
      i,
      " of ",
      length(wage_series_batches)
    )

    get_n_series_table(
      wage_series_batches[[i]],
      start_year = 2000,
      end_year = 2024,
      api_key = bls_api_key
    )
  }
)



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CLEAN AND COMBINE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ecec_wage_raw_list_clean <- map(
  ecec_wage_raw_list,
  ~ .x %>%
    select(
      year,
      period,
      where(is.numeric)
    )
)

ecec_wages_raw <- reduce(
  ecec_wage_raw_list_clean,
  full_join,
  by = c("year", "period")
)

dim(ecec_wages_raw)



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# LONG-FORM ECEC WAGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ecec_wages_quarterly <- ecec_wages_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(year, period),
    names_to = "series_id",
    values_to = "wage_cost_per_hour"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    wage_cost_per_hour = as.numeric(wage_cost_per_hour)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    wage_series_lookup,
    by = "series_id"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry),
    !is.na(estimate_code)
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    period,
    industry_code
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    period,
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    series_id,
    wage_cost_per_hour
  )


dim(ecec_wages_quarterly)

head(ecec_wages_quarterly)

ecec_wages_quarterly %>%
  count(industry)

ecec_wages_quarterly %>%
  count(year, period) %>%
  summarise(
    min_n = min(n),
    max_n = max(n),
    median_n = median(n)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# ANNUAL ECEC WAGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ecec_wages_annual <- ecec_wages_quarterly %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    industry_code,
    industry,
    estimate_code,
    series_id
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    wage_cost_per_hour = if (all(is.na(wage_cost_per_hour))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(wage_cost_per_hour, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    n_quarters = sum(!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
